The '''United States Penitentiary, Beaumont''' ('''USP Beaumont''') is a [[high security]] United States [[federal prison]] for male inmates in [[unincorporated area|unincorporated]] [[Jefferson County, Texas|Jefferson County]], [[Texas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www2.census.gov/geo/maps/DC2020/DC20BLK/st48_tx/county/c48245_jefferson/DC20BLK_C48245.pdf|title=2020 CENSUS - CENSUS BLOCK MAP: Jefferson County, TX|publisher=[[U.S. Census Bureau]]|access-date=2022-08-14|quote=Federal Correctional Complex Beaumont|pages=13-14 (PDF p. 14-15/50)}}</ref> It is part of the [[Federal Correctional Complex, Beaumont]] (FCC Beaumont) and is operated by the [[Federal Bureau of Prisons]], a division of the [[United States Department of Justice]].

FCC Beaumont is located approximately {{convert|100|mi|km}} east of [[Houston]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bop.gov/locations/institutions/bmp/index.jsp |title=USP Beaumont |publisher=Bop.gov |date=2015-04-10 |access-date=2015-10-12}}</ref>

==Incidents==
=== 1998 inmate murder ===
On September 10, 1998, inmate Ellis Joseph Mosher stabbed fellow inmate Stanley Moseley to death in a housing unit. Mosher stabbed Moseley multiple times with a 13-inch improvised blade in full view of correctional officers on duty. Mosher was serving a 20-year sentence for [[kidnapping]], while Moseley was serving a 15-year sentence for [[bank robbery]]. Mosher's defense claimed that Moseley had attacked him and raped him on previous occasions. Mosher's attorneys stated that he faced an imminent threat being housed with Moseley and had no alternative but to attack him. Mosher was sentenced to life in prison in 2008, he is currently housed at [[ADX Florence]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=death penalty news—-TEXAS – TCADP |url=https://tcadp.org/2008/02/08/death-penalty-news-texas/ |access-date=2023-08-04 |website=tcadp.org}}</ref>

=== 1999 inmate murder ===
On December 16, 1999, inmates Arzell Gulley and David Lee Jackson began arguing with another inmate, Darryl Brown. The argument resulted in Gulley and Jackson chasing Brown into a housing unit with "shanks", until they cornered him in a cell. The duo then stabbed Brown a total of 11 times, killing him. An autopsy found that a single knife strike hit Brown's left lung, resulting in his death. Gulley and Jackson were both indicted for the murder of Brown in 2005. Gulley was sentenced to life in prison and Jackson was sentenced to death. Jackson's death sentence was overturned and he was re-sentenced to life imprisonment after it was determined that the government withheld evidence in his trial. Gulley is currently serving his sentence at [[United States Penitentiary, Hazelton|USP Hazelton]], while Jackson is at [[Federal Correctional Complex, Yazoo City|FCI Yazoo City]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=FindLaw's United States Fifth Circuit case and opinions. |url=https://caselaw.findlaw.com/us-5th-circuit/1373966.html |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=Findlaw |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== 2001 inmate murder ===
On January 5, 2001, inmate Luther Plant was beaten and stomped to death by inmate Shannon Wayne Agofsky in an exercise cage. Plant was serving a 15-year sentence for drug offences while Agofsky was serving a life sentence for armed robbery of a bank, and the subsequent kidnapping and murder of the bank president in [[Noel, Missouri]]. The autopsy revealed that Plant suffered numerous injuries including a crushed neck, abrasions on his head, a broken jaw and nose, hemorrhaging around both eyes, four broken teeth, and internal bleeding in the lungs, trachea, esophagus, and stomach. Agofsky was transferred to [[ADX Florence]] before being convicted and sentenced to death for Plant's murder in 2004. He was on death row at [[United States Penitentiary, Terre Haute|USP Terre Haute]] until December 2024, when [[Joe Biden|President Joe Biden]] commuted Agofsky's death sentence (and those of 36 other inmates on federal death row) to life in prison.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FindLaw's United States Fifth Circuit case and opinions |url=https://caselaw.findlaw.com/us-5th-circuit/1329154.html |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=Findlaw |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2004-07-16 |title=Inmate sentenced to death in prison slaying |url=https://www.myplainview.com/news/article/Inmate-sentenced-to-death-in-prison-slaying-8924114.php |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=Plainview Herald |language=en-US}}</ref> Agofsky subsequently attempted to refuse the commutation as it would likely interfere with his ongoing appeal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Two death row inmates reject Biden's commutation of their life sentences |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/two-death-row-inmates-reject-bidens-commutation-life-sentences-rcna186235 |date=January 6, 2025 |work=NBC News}}</ref> In September 2025, Agofsky was transferred back to ADX Florence.

=== 2005 inmate murder ===
On May 7, 2005, inmates Marwin Mosley and Joseph Ebron entered the cell of inmate Keith Barnes where Ebron held Barnes down as Mosley stabbed him 106 times, killing him. Barnes was incarcerated for murder and conspiracy to rob, however, he became a target for Mosley and Ebron due to his testimony against a co-defendant for a reduced sentence. Mosley committed suicide in prison in 2006, and Ebron was charged with first-degree murder in the case and sentenced to death in 2009. Additionally, Michael Bacote, the inmate who acted as the lookout during the homicide was charged with second-degree murder and sentenced to 28 years in prison. Ebron was housed on death row at [[United States Penitentiary, Terre Haute|USP Terre Haute]] but had his sentenced commuted to life imprisonment by President Joe Biden, while Bacote is serving his sentence at [[United States Penitentiary, Allenwood|USP Allenwood]]. Ebron was transferred to [[ADX Florence]] following his commutation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=U.S. v. Ebron, CRIMINAL ACTION NO. 1:08-CR-36 {{!}} Casetext Search + Citator |url=https://casetext.com/case/us-v-ebron |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220722212843/https://casetext.com/case/us-v-ebron |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 22, 2022 |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=casetext.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-05-19 |title=Man condemned for killing fellow inmate |url=https://www.chron.com/news/houston-texas/article/Man-condemned-for-killing-fellow-inmate-1741090.php |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=Chron |language=en-US}}</ref>

===2007 inmate murder===
On November 28, 2007, correction officers were escorting inmates Mark Snarr (11093-081) and Edgar Garcia (28132-177) to their cells at the USP Beaumont.  When they arrived, Snarr and Garcia slipped from their restraints, repeatedly stabbed both correction officers with homemade prison knives known as [[Shiv (weapon)|shanks]], and took the officers' cell keys.

Snarr and Garcia then unlocked the cell of inmate Gabriel Rhone (09304-007) and stabbed Rhone over 50 times.  Additional officers arrived and used chemical agents to stop the attack, which lasted several minutes and was captured on surveillance camera.  The wounded corrections officers and Rhone were transported to a local hospital, where Rhone was pronounced dead. The officers were treated and survived.

Attorneys for Snarr and Garcia claimed that Rhone had repeatedly threatened to kill their clients and that prison officials had failed to respond to those threats.  However, Snarr and Garcia were subsequently convicted of murder and both were sentenced to death on May 24, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|author=Ken Fountain |url=http://www.beaumontenterprise.com/news/article/2-denied-self-defense-in-inmate-killing-731670.php |title=2 denied self-defense in inmate killing |publisher=Beaumont Enterprise |date=2010-03-29 |access-date=2015-10-12}}</ref><ref>[https://www.justice.gov/usao/txe/News/2010/EDTX_MURDER_SNARR_GARCIA052410.html] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120115123940/http://www.justice.gov/usao/txe/News/2010/EDTX_MURDER_SNARR_GARCIA052410.html|date=January 15, 2012}}</ref> They were both held on death row at [[United States Penitentiary, Terre Haute|USP Terre Haute]] until their death sentences were commuted by President Joe Biden in December 2024. Snarr and Garcia were then transferred to [[ADX Florence]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bop.gov/iloc2/InmateFinderServlet?Transaction=IDSearch&needingMoreList=false&IDType=IRN&IDNumber=11093-081&x=88&y=6 |title=Inmate Locator |publisher=Bop.gov |access-date=2015-10-12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bop.gov/iloc2/InmateFinderServlet?Transaction=IDSearch&needingMoreList=false&IDType=IRN&IDNumber=28132-177&x=78&y=8 |title=Inmate Locator |publisher=Bop.gov |access-date=2015-10-12}}</ref>

===2008 inmate murder===
On February 12, 2008, USP Beaumont staff discovered the body of a 29-year-old inmate, Ronald Joseph, in his cell. An autopsy showed that Joseph died from asphyxia due to ligature strangulation or compression of the neck. Further investigation identified James Sweeney (58827-066) and Harry Lee Napper (32403-037), both inmates at USP Beaumont, as suspects in the murder. Sweeney and Napper were indicted and charged with [[first-degree murder]], [[conspiracy (crime)|conspiracy]] to commit murder, and [[second-degree murder]] on May 4, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fbi.gov/houston/press-releases/2011/federal-inmates-charged-with-murdering-beaumont-prisoner |title=FBI — Federal Inmates Charged with Murdering Beaumont Prisoner |publisher=Fbi.gov |access-date=2015-10-12}}</ref> In 2012, Sweeney pleaded guilty to [[racketeering]] and murder charges for leading the prison gang [[Dead Man Incorporated]] in exchange for the murder charge being dismissed and was sentenced to life in prison.<ref>{{cite web|author=Justin Fenton |url=http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2012-09-26/news/bs-md-ci-sweeney-dmi-letter-20120926_1_plea-agreement-prison-gang-maryland-prisons |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130610055656/http://articles.baltimoresun.com/2012-09-26/news/bs-md-ci-sweeney-dmi-letter-20120926_1_plea-agreement-prison-gang-maryland-prisons |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 10, 2013 |title=Prison gang leader pleads guilty, promises to continue to defy government - tribunedigital-baltimoresun |publisher=Articles.baltimoresun.com |date=2012-09-26 |access-date=2015-10-12}}</ref><ref>[https://www.justice.gov/usao/txe/News/2012/EDTX_Sweeny_Totorice_Batte(Corrected)_%20092612.html] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130721041117/http://www.justice.gov/usao/txe/News/2012/EDTX_Sweeny_Totorice_Batte(Corrected)_%20092612.html|date=July 21, 2013}}</ref> Napper received a decades-long sentence.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bop.gov/iloc2/InmateFinderServlet?Transaction=NameSearch&needingMoreList=false&FirstName=harry&Middle=&LastName=napper&Race=U&Sex=U&Age=&x=0&y=0 |title=Inmate Locator |publisher=Bop.gov |access-date=2015-10-12}}</ref> Sweeney is now at [[United States Penitentiary, Terre Haute|USP Terre Haute]] and Napper is at [[ADX Florence]].

=== 2014 inmate murder ===
On March 3, 2014, inmates Ricky Fackrell and Christopher Cramer stabbed inmate Leo Johns to death. Fackrell, Cramer, and Johns were all members of the [[white supremacist]] prison gang [[Soldiers of Aryan Culture|Soldiers of Aryan Culture (SAC)]]. Fackrell and Cramer decided they needed to punish Johns for gambling and drinking, activities that are prohibited for SAC members. Defense counsel for Fackrell claimed that the men only agreed to assault Johns, however, both men were convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder and sentenced to death in 2018. Fackrell and Cramer were initially housed at [[ADX Florence]], but transferred to [[United States Penitentiary, Terre Haute|USP Terre Haute]] after sentencing. Following their commutations by President Joe Biden in 2024, they were transferred back to ADX Florence.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-06-13 |title=White Supremacists Sentenced to Death for Murdering Fellow Inmate at Texas Prison |url=https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/white-supremacists-sentenced-death-murdering-fellow-inmate-texas-prison |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=Justice.gov |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=United States v. Fackrell, No. 18-40598 {{!}} Casetext Search + Citator |url=https://casetext.com/case/united-states-v-fackrell-1 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220722212844/https://casetext.com/case/united-states-v-fackrell-1 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 22, 2022 |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=casetext.com}}</ref>

===2022 fatal altercation===
On the morning of Monday, January 31, 2022, multiple [[MS-13]] members began attacking associates of the [[Mexican Mafia]] and the [[Sureños|Surenos]]. Although officers responded quickly, four inmates were severely injured and taken to the hospital. Of them, 34-year-old Andrew Pineda and 54-year-old Guillermo Riojas would later be pronounced dead. 
In the aftermath of the deadly fight, the [[United States Bureau of Prisons]] enacted a lockdown across the entire Federal Prison network.<ref>[https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/federal-prisons-locked-coast-coast-deadly-fight-texas-facility-rcna14308 “Federal prisons remain locked down from coast to coast after deadly fight in Texas”] Dennis Romero and Michael Kosnar, [[NBC News]]</ref><ref>[https://www.fox4news.com/news/us-federal-prisons-on-lockdown-after-2-texas-inmates-killed/ “Two Texas inmates killed at Beaumont federal prison in fight involving MS-13”], Michael Balsamo and Michael R. Sisak, Fox 4/[[WKDA]]</ref> On April 7, 2022, 7 members of MS-13 were charged with racketeering conspiracy, murder in aid of racketeering, and other offences related to the brawl. The indictment named Juan Carlos Rivas-Moreiera, Dimas Alfaro-Granados, Rual Landaverde-Giron, Larry Navarete, Jorge Parada, Hector Ramires, and Sergio Sibrian as defendants.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-07 |title=7 MS-13 MEMBERS CHARGED WITH DOUBLE MURDER INSIDE FEDERAL PENITENTIARY IN BEAUMONT, TEXAS RESULTING IN NATIONWIDE LOCKDOWN OF FEDERAL PRISON SYSTEM |url=https://www.justice.gov/usao-edtx/pr/7-ms-13-members-charged-double-murder-inside-federal-penitentiary-beaumont-texas |access-date=2022-07-22 |website=Justice.gov |language=en}}</ref>

==Notable inmates==
* [[Joel Cacace]] - [[consigliere]] of the [[Colombo crime family]], pleaded guilty to [[racketeering]], [[extortion]], [[illegal gambling]], and participating in four murders in 2004; released on May 22, 2020, after serving 17 years of a 20-year sentence
* [[Willis Mark Haynes]] - serving a life sentence plus 45 years for shooting and killing three women on the [[Patuxent Research Refuge]] in [[Prince George's County, Maryland]]. His accomplice, [[Dustin Higgs]], received a death sentence for his involvement in the crime, and was executed on [[List of people executed in the United States in 2021|January 16, 2021]].
* Oscar Ramiro Ortega-Hernandez - serving a 25-year sentence for perpetrating the [[2011 White House shooting]], an attempt to kill President [[Barack Obama]]; pleaded guilty to terrorism and weapons offenses for using a [[Semi-automatic rifle|semi-automatic]] [[rifle]]; scheduled for release on June 21, 2033; transferred to [[Federal Correctional Institution, Herlong|FCI Herlong]]{{citation needed|date=February 2024}}
* [[Richard Scrushy]] - Founder of  [[HealthSouth Corporation]] who was convicted of bribery, conspiracy, and mail fraud.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.wbrc.com/story/19112961/richard-scrushys-prison-sentence-ends/|title=Richard Scrushy's prison sentence ends|website=Wbrc.com|date=July 25, 2012|access-date=August 1, 2024}}</ref>
* [[Steve Stockman|Stephen Ernest Stockman]] - former [[United States Representative]] for [[Texas's 36th congressional district]] sentenced for [[money laundering]], [[mail and wire fraud]], and falsification of records; served 2 years of a 10-year sentence, received a presidential pardon from [[Donald Trump]] on December 22, 2020
* [[Oscar Wyatt]] - founder of the [[Coastal Corporation]] in Texas; pleaded guilty in 2007 to [[wire fraud]] for paying [[kickbacks]] to [[Saddam Hussein]]'s regime to win oil contracts from Iraq; part of the [[United Nations]] [[Oil-for-Food Programme|Oil-for-Food Program]] debacle;<ref>{{cite web|last=Kearney |first=Christine |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-un-iraq-trial-idUSN2751695120071127 |title=Texas oilman Wyatt sentenced to year in prison |publisher=Reuters |date=November 27, 2007 |access-date=October 12, 2015}}</ref> released from custody on November 14, 2008; served 1 year at the minimum-security prison camp<ref>{{cite web|last1=Fowler|first1=Tom|title=Oscar Wyatt reports to prison in Beaumont|url=http://www.chron.com/business/article/Oscar-Wyatt-reports-to-prison-in-Beaumont-1614552.php|website=Houston Chronicle|publisher=[[Hearst Newspapers, LLC]]|access-date=October 9, 2022|date=January 2, 2008|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080103173430/http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/front/5420278.html|archivedate=January 3, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* Orlando Garcia - Found guilty of facilitation of first-degree murder in the murder of Tennessee State Trooper Calvin Jenks in January 2007 and sentenced to 19 years.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.actionnews5.com/story/6006296/teen-suspect-in-trooper-murder-admits-i-didnt-think-twice-about-shooting-him/ | title=Teen suspect in Trooper murder admits "I didn't think twice about shooting him"|website=Actionnews5.com | date=30 January 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://thecinemaholic.com/calvin-jenks-murder-where-are-alejandro-gauna-and-orlando-garcia-now/ | title=Calvin Jenks Murder: Where Are Alejandro Gauna and Orlando Garcia Now?|website=Thecinenaholic.com | date=4 May 2022 }}</ref>
* [[Patrick Franklin Andrews]] - Serial killer who murdered fellow prisoner while serving 35-year-to-life sentence for two murders committed in [[Washington, D.C.]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-04-13 |title=Office of Public Affairs {{!}} Federal Inmate Sentenced to Life in Prison for Murder of Fellow Prisoner {{!}} United States Department of Justice |url=https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/federal-inmate-sentenced-life-prison-murder-fellow-prisoner |access-date=2025-04-21 |website=Justice.gov |language=en}}</ref>
